daily_brief: Tensions within the European Union escalated significantly as Spain imposed border controls on travelers from Italy in retaliation for Rome's earlier restrictions, a dispute triggered by the mass influx of approximately 78,000 migrants into the Spanish enclave of Ceuta [BBC, The Guardian, Globe and Mail]. The crisis has fractured Schengen solidarity and pitted Spain's socialist government against Italy's conservative leadership. Meanwhile, Russian missile strikes killed three people including a child near Kyiv, continuing Moscow's intensified bombardment of the Ukrainian capital [BBC, France 24]. President Zelensky arrived in Belgrade for a landmark visit seeking broader support from traditionally Russia-friendly Serbia. In the Democratic Republic of Congo, Ebola cases surpassed 4,000 with health officials expressing concern the virus may be mutating, making this the second-largest outbreak on record [The Guardian, France 24]. A tragic school shooting in Thailand left eight dead, prompting the prime minister to pledge stricter gun control legislation [BBC]. In a significant Middle East development, the U.S. indicated progress toward a deal with Iran and Oman to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, while Saudi Arabia, Turkey, and Pakistan signed a historic mutual defense pact [The Hindu].

top_stories.headline: Spain and Italy Impose Reciprocal Border Controls as Ceuta Migration Crisis Fractures EU Unity
bullets: Spain imposed border controls on all air and sea travel from Italy starting midnight Saturday, lasting until September 7, in direct retaliation for Italy's similar restrictions imposed a week earlier
The crisis was triggered by approximately 78,000 migrants crossing from Morocco into the Spanish exclave of Ceuta on July 30-31 in an unprecedented mass rush
Italy stated it would maintain its controls until at least August 15, citing security concerns and expectations of another migration wave, while refusing to accept what it called Spanish 'ultimatums'
Spain's foreign minister described Italy's measures as 'a torpedo fired at the hull of European unity' and called them discriminatory against Spanish citizens

sources.name: BBC World
sources.framing_note: Emphasized the political dimension, framing it as a clash between Spain's socialist leader and Italy's conservative leader

sources.name: The Guardian
sources.framing_note: Highlighted the threat to Schengen and EU unity, quoted Spain's foreign minister extensively

sources.name: RFI English
sources.framing_note: Connected the crisis to Italy's broader proposal for migrant 'return hubs' outside the EU, including talks with Rwanda

sources.name: Globe and Mail
sources.framing_note: Straightforward factual reporting focused on the timeline and reciprocal nature of measures

top_stories.headline: Russian Missile Strikes Kill Three Near Kyiv as Zelensky Makes Historic Visit to Serbia
bullets: Ballistic missile strikes on Brovary district northeast of Kyiv killed three people including a child and wounded three others early Saturday morning
Falling debris damaged apartment buildings and vehicles, while fires broke out at multiple locations including a warehouse and fuel tank in Kyiv
President Zelensky arrived in Belgrade for his first visit to Serbia, seeking to build wider support from a country that has refused to apply sanctions against Russia
The attack comes days after strikes across Ukraine killed 21 people, with Zelensky citing delays in receiving anti-ballistic systems from partners as contributing to casualties

sources.name: BBC World
sources.framing_note: Combined the attack coverage with context about Zelensky's Serbia visit and Ukraine's appeals for faster weapons delivery

sources.name: France 24
sources.framing_note: Emphasized the escalation pattern, noting Moscow has 'significantly upped its attacks' in recent months

top_stories.headline: Ebola Outbreak in DRC Passes 4,000 Cases as Officials Warn Virus May Be Mutating
bullets: The Bundibugyo strain Ebola outbreak has reached 3,973 confirmed cases and 1,801 deaths as of August 4, with Africa CDC confirming cases topped 4,000
The outbreak is now the second-largest on record, with eight times more cases and six times more deaths than were recorded 11 weeks into the 2014-18 West Africa outbreak
Africa CDC and WHO officials announced plans to study whether the virus is mutating, citing the 'unprecedented' severity of this Bundibugyo outbreak
More than two-thirds of deaths are occurring in communities rather than treatment centers, prompting plans to go 'door to door' searching for patients

sources.name: The Guardian
sources.framing_note: Detailed reporting on mutation concerns and comparison to 2014 outbreak, quoted Africa CDC director extensively

sources.name: France 24
sources.framing_note: Brief video coverage describing it as a 'grim new milestone'

top_stories.headline: Thailand School Shooting Leaves Eight Dead; Prime Minister Pledges Stricter Gun Laws
bullets: A 14-year-old student killed his grandparents at their home before traveling to Debsirin School in Nonthaburi, where he shot and killed five teachers and injured 22 people before taking his own life
A student later died from injuries, bringing the total death toll to eight; the gun and bullets belonged to the teen's legally registered grandfather
Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul announced plans for new legislation restricting public firearm carrying to only government officials on duty
Thailand has approximately 10.3 million firearms in civilian possession, one of the highest rates in Southeast Asia, with about 4 million believed to be held illegally

sources.name: BBC World
sources.framing_note: Provided both policy response and witness accounts, including interviews with students who escaped

top_stories.headline: U.S. Signals Progress on Strait of Hormuz Deal as Saudi Arabia, Turkey, and Pakistan Sign Defense Pact
bullets: A U.S. official reported progress between Iran and Oman toward reopening the Strait of Hormuz, stating Washington expects a deal soon that would allow the U.S. to lift its blockade of Iranian ports
Saudi Arabia, Turkey, and Pakistan signed the Mecca Joint Defence Agreement, declaring that an armed attack on any signatory would be treated as an attack on all three
The defense pact was signed amid ongoing Houthi attacks on Yemen's Marib province that killed at least 10 people Friday, including eight government forces and two civilians
Before the U.S.-Iran war began February 28, about one-fifth of global oil consumption transited the strait; its closure has caused energy prices to surge

sources.name: The Hindu
sources.framing_note: Comprehensive coverage linking Hormuz negotiations, the defense pact, and Houthi attacks as interconnected regional developments

sources.name: France 24
sources.framing_note: Focused on Houthi violence and escalation concerns in Yemen

Pope Leo XIV to meet clerical abuse survivors during September visit to France, his first papal state visit to the country since 2008

Spanish police arrest 78 people in dismantling of major Mediterranean drug and human smuggling network operating between Spain and Algeria
